newsitem.title: CHINA: China to invest 2.13 bln yuan in key grain bases.
newsitem.headline: China to invest 2.13 bln yuan in key grain bases.

text.p: China has decided to invest 2.13 billion yuan ($257 million) in the next five years to build 20 key grain producing bases, Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The State Planning Commission has given formal approval to a feasibility study on the plan, it quoted officials of the commission as saying.
The 20 bases would be in China's main grain producing areas, including southwestern Sichuan province, northeastern Heilongjiang and Jilin and eastern Shandong province, it said.
The report did not say specifically where the funds would be invested but normally such projects involve funds for growing, storage and transport.

The investment would shared by the central and local governments, including one billion yuan in capital investments in the state budget, it said. The central government has already allocated 200 million yuan for investment in 1996.
Grain output of the 20 production areas totalled 79 million tonnes in 1995. China produced 466 million tonnes of grain in 1995.
Grain output by the key regions is expected to reach 90 million tonnes in the year 2000, accounting for 18 percent of the national total, the agency said. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
